payload.text: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.

IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

13. TERM OF AGREEMENT. This Agreement will take effect on the Effective Date and remain in effect for a period of 1 year; provided, that Sections 2 and 3 level shall terminate promptly upon (a) any action or omission by Client or any of its customers which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it had pursuant to said Agreements or (b) any violations or breach by Client of Sections 8a - 8c. This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. If Client decides to discontinue its Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new name server within 30 days. In case of discontinued Service, Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content. If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.

14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.

15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
16. MODIFICATIONS. This Agreement may be amended at any time and from time to time, but any amendment must be in writing and signed by the party to be charged.

17. WAIVER. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement will be valid unless it is in writing and signed by the party against whom it is sought to be enforced. No waiver at any time of any provision of this Agreement will be deemed a waiver of any other provision of this
-8- 9 Agreement at that time or a waiver of that or any other provision of this Agreement at any other time.
18. UNDEFINED TERMS. Terms that are not specifically defined in this Agreement are used as set forth in the California Uniform Commercial Code.

19. POWER AND AUTHORITY. Each party represents to the other that it has all necessary power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Agreement. The individuals executing this Agreement on behalf of each party represent that they have authority to do so.

20. NOTICES. All notices required or permitted to be sent under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be sent to the parties at the addresses set forth in the preamble of this Agreement, or to such other addresses and to such other individuals of which either party may notify the other in a notice which complies with the provisions of this subsection. All notices will be deemed given (i) when delivered by hand, (ii) one (l) day after delivery to a reputable overnight carrier, or (iii) three (3) days after placement in first-class mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested.
21. CUMULATIVE RIGHTS. The rights and remedies of the parties hereunder are cumulative and are in addition to, and not in lieu of, all rights and remedies available at law and in equity.
22. CAPTIONS. The captions in this Agreement are included for convenience of reference only and will not be construed to define or limit any of the provisions contained herein.

23. JOINT DRAFTING AND NEUTRAL CONSTRUCTION. This Agreement is a negotiated document and shall be deemed to have been drafted jointly by the Parties, and no rule of construction or interpretation shall apply against any particular party based on a contention that the Agreement was drafted by one of the Parties including, but not limited to California Civil Code section 1654, the provisions of which are hereby waived. This Agreement shall be construed and interpreted in a neutral manner.

24. VALIDITY OF AGREEMENT. If any term, provision, covenant, or condition of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and shall in no way be affected or invalidated. The provisions of Sections 1 and 5 through 30 this Agreement will survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

25. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement, including all Exhibits, contains the entire agreement of the Parties relating to the rights granted and obligations assumed herein. Any oral representations or modifications concerning this instrument shall be of no force or effect unless contained in a subsequent written modification signed by the party to be charged.

paragraphs.text: 10. CONFIDENTIALITY.

a. Client acknowledges its responsibility to preserve the confidentiality of certain technology, information, and documentation embedded in the Interface and agrees to respect the confidential nature of the Interface. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, it is understood and agreed that Client's confidentiality obligations relating to any System and any data, documentation, or other output from such System shall include those specified in any agreements between Client and the licensor of the System.

b. TrueLink acknowledges its responsibilities to preserve the confidentiality of all results of the Support Services, Client's Intellectual Property, and subject to Section 8(d) herein Client Confidential Information.

c. The parties hereto recognize that certain of the information and documentation previously provided or that may in the future be provided by a party to the other related to the matters covered by this Agreement includes privileged, confidential and proprietary information belonging to such party (a party's "Proprietary Information") which, if disclosed, could result in substantial and irreparable harm to such party. For information and documentation to qualify as a party's Proprietary Information, such information must either be marked "Confidential" or otherwise identified in writing as confidential at or prior to the time of its delivery to the other hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will automatically be deemed TrueLink Proprietary Information, whether or not specifically marked or designated as such:

(i) any implementation information or user's guides for the Interface, (ii) any advance releases of TrueLink promotional material, (iii) information concerning TrueLink's business plans and strategies, and (iv) TrueLink's customer list. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will be automatically deemed Client Proprietary Information: Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services, including any information or materials of any type or nature, tangible or intangible, disclosed by Client as a result of the TrueLink's relationship with Client relating to the business, products or technology or potential business, products or technology of Client, business plans, financial information, borrower and loan data technical specifications, design concepts,

-6- 7 technical information, customer lists, pricing information, marketing plans and other similar information pertaining to Client. Each agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials as strictly confidential, except to the extent otherwise agreed by the other in writing. Except to the extent otherwise agreed by both parties in writing, party further agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials which it prepares using or based on the other's Proprietary information or any portion thereof (the "Derivative Documentation") as strictly confidential, including, without limitation, any notes made and all reports prepared in connection with this Agreement.

d. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the restrictions on disclosure and other obligations set forth above with respect to Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation shall not apply when, and to the extent that such Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public through no fault of the receiving party; (ii) was previously known to the receiving party free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iii) is subsequently disclosed to the receiving party by a third party who may transfer and disclose such information without restriction and free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iv) is independently developed by the receiving party or a third party without reference to or any use of the

disclosing party's proprietary information; or (v) is required to be disclosed by the receiving party as a matter of law, provided that the receiving party uses all reasonable efforts to provide the disclosing party with at least ten days' prior notice of such disclosure.

11. STANDARD OF CARE. TrueLink shall perform the Hosting and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services for Client with the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The § 2(a) grant runs to Client alone: neither affiliates nor contractors acting on Client's behalf are named, and nothing in §§ 1-2 provides a mechanism to add them (the Exhibit A amendment right in § 2(b)(ii) covers sites, not entities). The fallback position (affiliates covered, at minimum on written notice) is therefore not met, so this is a material deviation rather than a minor wording gap. Transfer is also constrained: § 15 requires the other party's consent with a carve-out only for assignment to a financially responsible affiliate, and no successor/M&A carve-out, so the fallback's successor-transfer element also fails. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion (it runs until termination under § 12, with automatic termination of §§ 2-3 in § 13 tied to defined uncured breaches), so this is not walk-away territory; the licence being subscription-style rather than perpetual is consistent with the bargain and is not flagged. The redline extends the grant to affiliates and contractors and adds a mutual successor-transfer carve-out.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and a read of the general/miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13-30, p0078-p0097) confirms there is no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement. TrueLink is a hosting vendor that operates Client's web site and processes consumer mortgage and credit-repository data, so the absence of any coverage requirement is walk-away territory under the rule (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data). Inserted a new Section 31 immediately after the final miscellaneous provision (Force Majeure) at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request; the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment. Note that the survival clause at p0090 refers to "Sections 1 and 5 through 30" and would ideally be conformed to include the new section, but that is a minor drafting point rather than a separate deviation.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry commercial general liability, professional liability (E&O) and cyber liability insurance, with certificates on request.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision, so we added standard coverages appropriate for a vendor that hosts our web site and processes consumer credit data, together with certificates on request. If USD 5,000,000 cyber cover is not currently in place, we can accept E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber of USD 2,000,000.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical, ip-data).**

- **What's wrong:** §2(d) "Ownership" (p0029) only protects TrueLink — it confirms TrueLink retains all ownership in the Interface but says nothing about Client's side. There is no statement that Client retains its Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, or borrower/customer data, and the "TrueLink's Intellectual Property" definition (p0017) sweeps in *improvements, materials, data, programs, subroutines, tools* associated with the Interface — so Support Services work product Client pays for could vest in the Vendor with neither assignment nor a licence back. That fails even the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables).
- **Not a substitute:** confidentiality treatment of Client IP and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Client Proprietary Information (p0065) is a non-disclosure protection, not ownership; the retained ownership of domains and Client Content at p0078 applies only on discontinuation of the Hosting Service.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** one insertion into §2(d) adding (i) Client's retention of Client Content, Client IP and all borrower/applicant/customer data including Credit Data, with no assignment and no joint ownership; and (ii) assignment of Support Services deliverables to Client with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back for embedded TrueLink IP. TrueLink's Interface ownership is left untouched.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the broad §8(d) Credit Data licence ("license, resell, exploit") is a negotiated carve-out confined to aged raw third-party credit data not combined with Client Proprietary Information and subject to the Non-Competition Agreement, so the redline expressly preserves it rather than reopening that bargain.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only ownership provision (§2(d)) is one-directional: it confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface but nowhere states that Client retains ownership of Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property or its borrower/customer data. The TrueLink Intellectual Property definition (p0017) sweeps in "improvements... materials... data, know-how... programs, subroutines, tools" associated with the Interface, so Support Services work product created and paid for by Client could vest in TrueLink with no assignment and no licence back — failing both the preferred and the fallback position (which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). Confidentiality treatment of Client's IP and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Client Proprietary Information (p0065) is a non-disclosure protection, not an ownership allocation, and the retained ownership of domains/Client Content on termination (p0078) is limited to the discontinuation scenario. Redline adds the Customer Data/IP retention sentence, an assignment of Support Services deliverables with a licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, and a no-joint-ownership statement, leaving TrueLink's Interface ownership intact. Noted but not separately flagged: the broad §8(d) licence to "license, resell, exploit" Credit Data is a negotiated carve-out limited to aged raw third-party credit data not combined with Client Proprietary Information and is subject to the Non-Competition Agreement, so we preserve it expressly rather than reopen it.

Original paragraphs:
p0029: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
p0017: f. TrueLink's Intellectual Property. The term "TrueLink Intellectual Property" means any or its intellectual property associated with the Interface, including, without limitation, designs, formulas, procedures, methods, apparatus, ideas, creations, improvements, works of authorship, materials, processes, inventions, techniques, data, know-how, show-how, algorithms, programs, subroutines, tools, patents and patentable materials, copyrights and copyrightable materials and trade secrets.
p0054: d. Use of Credit Data during the term of this Agreement. Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
Client: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.
TrueLink: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.

Rendered redline:
p0029: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface. Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and all data of Client and of its borrowers, loan applicants, customers and brokers (including Credit Data), and nothing in this Agreement operates as an assignment or transfer to TrueLink of any of the foregoing or creates any joint ownership therein, other than the license granted under Section 8(d). TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest in any deliverables and work product created specifically for Client in the course of the Support Services, excluding TrueLink's Intellectual Property existing prior to or developed independently of such Support Services, in which TrueLink hereby grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense such TrueLink Intellectual Property to the extent embedded in such deliverables for the purposes of Client's business.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a sentence confirming that Client keeps ownership of its content, intellectual property and borrower/customer data, and that Support Services deliverables are assigned to Client with a licence back to any embedded TrueLink IP; our playbook requires that we own what we pay for and what we put in, with no assignment or joint ownership of our data. TrueLink's ownership of the Interface is untouched, and the existing Credit Data licence in Section 8(d) is expressly preserved.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rationale correctly declines walk-away treatment (no at-will revocation; termination tied to uncured breach) and correctly treats the subscription rather than perpetual term as a non-flagged sub-element.

Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position with a targeted edit: inserts 'its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf' into the grant and appends a successor/merger/asset-sale carve-out to § 15; the elevated changed-character ratios reflect necessary insertions rather than gratuitous rewriting.

**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I checked:
- Full-text search for "insurance" — zero hits across the document.
- Read the entire general/miscellaneous block (Sections 13–30, p0078–p0097) and the section outline; there is no insurance covenant, and no Exhibit carries one (Exhibits A and B are pricing placeholders, both "to be agreed").
- Confirmed "Customer Data" is not a defined term here, so the inserted clause uses the document's own terminology ("Client Content and any other data of Client or its customers").

Why it matters directionally: TrueLink is the hosting vendor operating our web site and processing consumer mortgage and credit-repository data. Combined with a vendor liability cap of 12 months' hosting/support fees (p0077), uninsured vendor exposure sits in the rule's walk-away territory.

The fix: a new Section 31 inserted after Force Majeure at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment as a landing zone.

One drafting point flagged in the rationale rather than as a separate deviation: the survival clause at p0090 reads "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so it should be conformed to pick up the new Section 31 — worth catching in the next turn of the document, since the clause requires coverage for one year post-term.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

ops.text: TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF CLIENT DATA. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including reasonable migration support for the Web Site and Hosting Services, for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Client Content and Client data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

As TrueLink hosts our site and holds our borrower and loan data, the current termination terms leave us responsible for re-hosting with no right to get our data back; we can discuss a 90-day assistance period if six months is not workable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client — customer side); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Section 5a imposes a monthly minimum fee for Hosting and Support Services, so the agreement is not at our preferred position of pure usage/ordered-services pricing. However, the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term (Section 13: one-year initial term, auto-renewing annually, terminable on 30 days' notice of non-renewal), and Section 14 gives Client a standalone right to terminate at any time, with services (and therefore fees) ending on the last day of the month following notice. There is no multi-year take-or-pay lock-in, no shortfall or penalty mechanic, and no volume cap on Client's usage. This sits at the playbook fallback and is acceptable, so no redline. Two points to note commercially rather than as deviations: the minimum dollar amounts are left blank and should be filled in (or deleted) at signature, and Section 6's carve-out barring Client from contesting or obtaining backup for the "minimum monthly fees" cross-references "Section 4" while the minimums actually appear in Section 5 — worth correcting for clarity.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

**What I found**

- **§9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** exists, but it is a pure Year 2000 date-processing warranty. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no services warranty, and no stated remedy period.
- **§11 "STANDARD OF CARE" (p0069)** requires only "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — self-referential, unbounded in time, and with no repair/re-perform/refund remedy. It does not reach the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
- **§8 (p0051, p0056)** imposes compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties on **Client only** — the mirror obligations on TrueLink are absent.
- **Disclaimer (p0076)** is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does *not* swallow express warranties. No carve-out edit was needed — the gap is the missing warranty itself, not an over-broad disclaimer. This also means we are not in walk-away "AS IS" territory.
- Searches for "conform" and "professional and workmanlike" returned nothing anywhere in the document, confirming no unlisted section carries a vendor performance warranty.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — inserts after p0060, into §9, at the **preferred** position: professional/workmanlike services; 12-month software conformance and 90-day services conformance; TrueLink compliance with laws; no malicious code; and repair/replacement/re-performance or refund of fees as Client's remedy. The comment offers the 90/30-day fallback as a negotiating concession.

One note recorded in the rationale rather than flagged separately: §4 (p0043) and §5 (p0045) contain unfilled blanks ("not less than ____ months", "$____ per month"), which is a separate commercial-completeness issue outside this rule.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only TrueLink warranty in the Agreement (Section 9) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty; there is no warranty that the Interface or related software conforms to its documentation, no professional/workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty from TrueLink, and no repair, re-performance or refund remedy. Section 11 (p0069) only requires TrueLink to use "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard with no fixed period and no remedy, which does not reach even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund). By contrast, Section 8 imposes compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties on Client only. The disclaimer at p0076 is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow an express warranty and needs no carve-out edit; the gap is the absence of the warranty itself. Redline inserts the preferred performance warranty and remedy into Section 9, with the fallback periods offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0059: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
p0060: (ii) will operate before, on and after January 1, 2000, in the processing of dates, including without limitation calculating, comparing, indexing and sequencing; and (iii) will successfully transition from December 31, 1999, to January 1, 2000, without human intervention. At Client's request, TrueLink will provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate adequate testing of the Interface and all related software to meet the foregoing requirements. Client will provide reasonable access to TrueLink make any repairs necessary to comply with this section and make any upgrades specified by TrueLink to so comply, all at TrueLink's sole cost and expense, to the extent such upgrades were not previously requested by Client pursuant to previously requested Hosting Services or Support Services as set forth herein.
p0069: 11. STANDARD OF CARE. TrueLink shall perform the Hosting and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services for Client with the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations.
p0076: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.

In addition, TrueLink represents and warrants that: (a) the Hosting Services, Support Services and any other agreed-upon services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with applicable industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications, and for a period of ninety (90) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to their descriptions in this Agreement and the Exhibits hereto; (c) TrueLink will comply in all material respects with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement; and (d) the Interface and all related software will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code. Client's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or services, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services.

input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation. Section 13 only makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days (and confirms Client's ownership of domains and Client Content), and Section 14 merely runs services to month-end after notice. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return or destruction mechanic at all. Nothing obliges TrueLink, which hosts the Web Site and holds Client borrower and loan data, to return that data in usable form, assist migration, or certify deletion — below even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days). We propose inserting the preferred language (6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion thereafter) as a new Section 14a, with a 90-day assistance period available as a fallback.

The agreement does contain a minimum commitment (Section 5a: monthly minimums for Hosting and Support Services), so it is not at our preferred usage-only position. But it clears the fallback comfortably:

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 5a imposes a monthly minimum fee for Hosting and Support Services, so the agreement is not at our preferred position of pure usage/ordered-services pricing. However, the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term (Section 13: one-year initial term, auto-renewing annually, terminable on 30 days' notice of non-renewal), and Section 14 gives Client a standalone right to terminate at any time, with services (and therefore fees) ending on the last day of the month following notice. There is no multi-year take-or-pay lock-in, no shortfall or penalty mechanic, and no volume cap on Client's usage. This sits at the playbook fallback and is acceptable, so no redline. Two points to note commercially rather than as deviations: the minimum dollar amounts are left blank and should be filled in (or deleted) at signature, and Section 6's carve-out barring Client from contesting or obtaining backup for the "minimum monthly fees" cross-references "Section 4" while the minimums actually appear in Section 5 — worth correcting for clarity.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings, redline positions and negotiation priorities

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of the 18 verified findings, **6 are deviations**, **2 are missing clauses**, and **10 are compliant** (several materially in our favour).

The commercial risk in this Agreement is concentrated in the ri[REDACTED] architecture, and it is skewed against us:

- **Liability is asymmetric in a walk-away way.** The only cap in the Agreement sits inside the indemnity section, limits TrueLink to 12 months' hosting and support compensation, and leaves Client — including under a very broad indemnity — entirely uncapped. There is no consequential damages exclusion anywhere in the document.
- **There is no vendor IP indemnity and no non-infringement warranty.** The only infringement references run against Client. TrueLink's indemnity is limited to claims arising from its own breach or failure to perform.
- **Ownership is one-directional.** §2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface but nowhere confirms that Client retains ownership of Client Content, Client IP or borrower/customer data; the broad TrueLink Intellectual Property definition could capture Support Services work product that Client paid for.
- **We have effectively no vendor performance warranty.** The only TrueLink warranty is a Year 2000 warranty; §11 offers only a self-referential standard of care with no period and no remedy.
- **We cannot get our data back on exit, and the vendor carries no insurance obligation.** Neither transition assistance/data return nor insurance appears anywhere in the Agreement, notwithstanding that TrueLink hosts our web site and processes consumer mortgage and credit-repository data.

On the positive side, the Agreement contains **no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or audit obligation binding Client**, **no liquidated damages or early-termination fee**, a **Client termination-for-convenience right**, a clean **12-month term with a 30-day non-renewal window**, and a **most-favoured-rate undertaking from TrueLink in §6**. We do not propose to reopen any of these.

We also note two housekeeping points that are not deviations: the termination provisions are mis-numbered and sit inside the block headed "§ 12 INDEMNITY" (§13 Term, §14 Termination), with §2c and §13 cross-referencing "Section 12" for termination; and §6's minimum-fee carve-out cross-references "Section 4" when the minimums appear in §5. Exhibits A and B remain blank and the monthly minimum dollar amounts must be populated or deleted at signature.

---

## Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Cap runs one way only (TrueLink limited to 12 months' compensation; Client uncapped). No consequential damages exclusion. Walk-away territory. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Materially one-sided; no vendor IP indemnity and no non-infringement warranty anywhere. Fails the fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | No retention of Client Content/IP/borrower data; Support Services work product may vest in TrueLink with no assignment or licence back. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No successor/M&A carve-out for Client and consent is at TrueLink's absolute discretion. No change-of-control right for TrueLink (that limb is fine). |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone — no affiliates or contractors, and no mechanism to add them; transfer also constrained. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | Non-exclusive licence; Client expressly free to acquire, develop or licence competing products. §3(i) credit-report tie is a narrow use-contingent term at the fallback. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by Client. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No competitive restraint on Client; §2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to build or buy competing services. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Client may terminate on notice with no cause and no fee (services to month-end following notice); TrueLink has no convenience right. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only TrueLink warranty is Year 2000; no conformance, services, compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Fails the fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No obligation on TrueLink to return data in usable form, assist migration or certify deletion. Below the fallback. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or records right over Client. Better than preferred; §3(e) gives us usage statistics and raw logs. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law, exclusive venue San Luis Obispo County. Sits at the fallback; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No Client-side MFN. §6 MFN runs in our favour, plus a one-year price freeze. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Monthly minimum confined to a 12-month auto-renewing term with a standalone Client exit right; no take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. Sits at the fallback. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-raiding covenant on Client. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-year renewals with a 30-day non-renewal window either way. Meets preferred; no reminder obligation and no uplift cap (minor). |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance covenant anywhere; vendor hosts our site and processes consumer credit data. Walk-away territory under the rule. |

---

## Walk-away items

These three items are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** The playbook expressly identifies "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as walk-away. We require a mutual, agreement-wide cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, the standard Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap.
2. **Prohibition on Client assignment with no M&A carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** A corporate transaction would currently require TrueLink's consent at its absolute discretion. We require a successor carve-out and a "not unreasonably withheld" standard.
3. **No insurance for a vendor processing personal data (INSURANCE).** A full-text search returns no hits for "insurance." We require CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

We would also treat the **absence of any vendor IP indemnity** (INDEMN) as effectively non-negotiable given the finding that the clause fails even the fallback and the only infringement references run against us.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two missing clauses, with the proposals as verified:
   - § 12(b): add IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct prongs to TrueLink's indemnity (smallest edit reaching the preferred position; the existing §12 cap language covering §§3, 4, 7 and 11 is left undisturbed).
   - § 2(d): add Client data/IP retention, assignment of Support Services deliverables with a licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, and a no-joint-ownership statement, preserving TrueLink's Interface ownership and the negotiated §8(d) Credit Data carve-out.
   - § 12 cap: make the cap mutual and agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with the standard uncapped carve-outs.
   - § 15: add the successor/M&A carve-out for Client and a reasonableness standard on consent.
   - § 2(a): extend the grant to Client affiliates and contractors and add a mutual successor-transfer carve-out.
   - § 9: add a TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with a repair, re-perform or refund remedy (fallback of 90 days software / 30 days services offered in the comment).
   - New § 14a: post-termination transition assistance (6 months at then-current rates), machine-readable data return within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter (90-day assistance available as a fallback).
   - New § 31: vendor insurance covenant, with the survival clause at §"1 and 5 through 30" conformed.
2. **Fallback authority.** Confirm negotiating authority to settle at: customary IP exclusions and remedies on the vendor IP indemnity; the 90-day transition assistance period; and E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M on insurance.
3. **Commercial completion.** Populate or delete Exhibits A and B and the blank monthly minimum service charge in § 5a before execution; the 12-month compensation cap measure only becomes meaningful once those charges are populated.
4. **Housekeeping pass.** Correct the § 2c and § 13 cross-references to "Section 12" (termination is § 14), and the § 6 cross-reference to "Section 4" (minimums are in § 5), and renumber the mis-headed § 12 block if the counterparty will accept it.
5. **Separate diligence.** Obtain and review the referenced **Non-Competition Agreement** — it is not part of this document and is invoked here only to limit TrueLink's use of Credit Data.
6. **Do not reopen.** No redline on exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, audit, liquidated damages, termination for convenience, renewal or governing law. On AUDIT specifically, we should resist any vendor attempt to introduce audit rights; if raised, only on the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).
7. **Flag for a future term extension.** If the term is ever extended beyond 12 months, revisit lengthening TrueLink's non-renewal notice to 90 days and adding a renewal reminder and a CPI/3% uplift cap."}

## Walk-away items

These three items are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** The playbook expressly identifies "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as walk-away. We require a mutual, agreement-wide cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, the standard Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap.
2. **Prohibition on Client assignment with no M&A carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** A corporate transaction would currently require TrueLink's consent at its absolute discretion. We require a successor carve-out and a "not unreasonably withheld" standard.
3. **No insurance for a vendor processing personal data (INSURANCE).** A full-text search returns no hits for "insurance." We require CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

We would also treat the **absence of any vendor IP indemnity** (INDEMN) as effectively non-negotiable given the finding that the clause fails even the fallback and the only infringement references run against us.
